title: Christ Is Supreme and Reconciles Through Death
summary_text: Thankful for their faith and love, Paul prays that the Colossians will know God's will and live to please Him. The gospel has taught them God's grace, and the Father gives the saints an inheritance through His Son, in whom they have redemption and forgiveness of sins. The Son shows the invisible God, is firstborn over creation, holds everything together, and heads the church; all things were created through and for Him, and all God's fullness dwells in Him. Through Christ's death, God has reconciled former enemies to present them holy, if they remain firm in faith. Paul suffers and works to make God's word known among the Gentiles: Christ in them brings hope of glory.
key_points: The gospel bears fruit among the Colossians, whose faith and love lead Paul to thank God.
Paul prays for wise, fruitful lives and thanks the Father for redemption and forgiveness through His Son.
The Son is firstborn over creation, and God makes peace through His blood on the cross.
God has reconciled them through Christ's death to present them holy, if they continue in faith.
Paul serves the church by revealing God's mystery among the Gentiles: Christ in them, bringing hope of glory.

title: Fullness in Christ Rather Than Human Rules
summary_text: Paul wants the believers united in love and firm in faith, protected from teaching that draws them away from Christ. God's fullness lives bodily in Christ, and believers are complete in Him. Paul describes their circumcision through Christ, burial with Him in baptism, and rising with Him through faith in God's power. Though dead in trespasses and sinful uncircumcision, they have been made alive and forgiven, with their debt removed through the cross. Paul rejects judgment over food or a Sabbath, angel worship, and harsh human rules that cannot restrain the flesh.
key_points: Paul urges firm faith in Christ rather than captivity to deceptive human teaching.
Christ contains God's fullness, and believers receive circumcision from Him, share His burial in baptism, and rise with Him through faith.
God gives life and forgives trespasses, removing the debt against believers and defeating hostile powers through the cross.
Paul opposes judgment about food and a Sabbath, along with angel worship that loses connection to Christ.
Human restrictions may look wise but cannot check indulgence of the flesh.

title: Living the New Life in Christ
summary_text: Because believers have risen with Christ, Paul directs their thoughts toward Him above and their coming share in His glory. They must put away sexual immorality, greed called idolatry, anger, and lies, since God's wrath is coming against disobedience. As God's elect and holy people, they are to forgive, love, let Christ's peace rule, and teach His word with thanks. Paul then addresses wives and husbands, children and fathers, calling for submission, love, obedience, and care that does not discourage children. Slaves must serve sincerely as serving Christ, who gives an inheritance and judges wrongdoing without favoritism.
key_points: Their life is hidden with Christ, and they will share His glory when He appears.
Paul commands them to abandon sexual sin, greed, anger, and lies as people renewed in their Creator's image.
God's holy people are to forgive, love, live in Christ's peace, and teach His word with gratitude.
Wives must submit, husbands must love, children must obey, and fathers must avoid discouraging their children.
Slaves must serve sincerely for Christ, who gives an inheritance and repays wrongdoing without favoritism.

title: Prayer, Wise Speech, and Fellow Workers
summary_text: Masters must treat slaves fairly because they too have a Master in heaven. Paul asks for watchful prayer and an opening to speak the word about Christ clearly, then urges wise conduct and gracious speech toward outsiders. He sends the faithful workers Tychicus and Onesimus with news and encouragement. Greetings include Epaphras, who prays earnestly for their maturity, and others who work with Paul. He directs churches to exchange letters, urges Archippus to finish his ministry, and ends with a request to remember his chains and a blessing of grace.
key_points: Masters owe slaves fair treatment because they themselves answer to a Master in heaven.
Paul requests prayer for clear speech about Christ and urges wisdom and grace in speaking with outsiders.
Tychicus and Onesimus will bring news, while Paul's fellow workers send greetings and Epaphras prays for the church.
